subject: Draft MAP: Data handling & compliance milestones for HealthTech evaluation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Draft MAP: Data handling & compliance milestones for HealthTech evaluation

Hi Emma — great conversation this morning. Per our call, attaching an initial Mutual Action Plan focused on the data handling and compliance milestones you highlighted. I want to make sure we capture the PHI/PII constraints and the audit / retention requirements up front so your security and legal teams can validate quickly.

Quick recap of the MAP milestones in this draft (attached: MAP_HealthTech_v0.1.pdf):

1) Requirement confirmation (owner: HealthTech Legal/Sec) — by 2026-04-02
   - Confirm classification of data types sent to Redwood (PHI, pseudonymized PII, non-sensitive logs)
   - Provide any mandatory retention/deletion SLAs (e.g., patient records vs request logs)

2) Architecture decision (owner: Redwood Solutions / HealthTech Sec) — by 2026-04-09
   - Decide: Hosted API (Redwood Hosted) vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
   - If PHI is in scope, confirm Private deployment or Dedicated with contractual controls

3) KMS / Key control integration (owner: HealthTech IT & Redwood Security) — by 2026-04-16
   - KMS/HSM requirements (bring-your-own-key? HSM-backed KMS?)
   - Key rotation, export controls, and access audit

4) Logging & audit trail spec (owner: HealthTech Sec & Redwood Infra) — by 2026-04-23
   - Event types to log (API requests, model selection, prompt hash, token-level metadata)
   - Retention windows per event type and support for eDiscovery/forensics

5) Compliance evidence handoff (owner: Redwood Security) — by 2026-04-30
   - Provide SOC 2 summary, pen-test report excerpt, and sample audit logs schema

Target commercial close: 2026-05-15 (tentative) — dependent on architecture decision above.

Open questions for your team (please reply inline):
- Do you require customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM) for PHI? If yes, any vendor constraints?
- Regulatory scope: is HIPAA the only regime, or do we need EU data residency for subset of traffic?
- Minimum required retention for any audit logs or model outputs (HealthTech legal to confirm)

Next steps: I'll push an updated MAP with action owners and dates based on your replies; Marissa (cc'd) will include a technical appendix with default retention values and audit log schema.

Attachments: MAP_HealthTech_v0.1.pdf (draft)

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Draft MAP: Data handling & compliance milestones for HealthTech evaluation

Thanks Ben — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side before legal signs off:

- PHI scope: yes, content from our clinician workflows includes PHI. We need to avoid any hosted multi-tenant processing for PHI unless it's under a BAA and supports BYOK/HSM. Private on-prem or VPC with customer-managed keys preferred.

- Retention: our baseline requirement is that patient-identifiable model outputs and raw requests must be deletable on demand and stored no longer than 180 days by default for production; we may need longer retention (up to 7 years) for audit cases — legal to confirm.

- Audit trails: need per-request immutable audit entries (timestamped, actor, operation, model version, token-level hashes). Can Redwood provide an exportable audit log in NDJSON or standard syslog format?

- eDiscovery & deletion: must support scoped deletion for an individual patient across all logs and persisted caches (including KV cache) — can you outline how deletions are propagated through your cache/batching layers?

Looping in Kyle from InfoSec to validate the above. If you can update the MAP with answers to the bolded questions and a concrete technical appendix, we can move the architecture decision forward.

Best,
Emma
Emma Johnson
Director of Product Security | HealthTech Inc.
emma.johnson@healthtech.io
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Draft MAP: Data handling & compliance milestones for HealthTech evaluation

Emma — thanks for the specifics. Quick technical notes to address your asks; I'll draft a short appendix to attach to the MAP.

- Deployment modes & PHI: Redwood supports Private (VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated (single-tenant GPU pools). For PHI in production we recommend Private or Dedicated with contractual controls + BAA. Private gives the most control over networking and data egress; we can support an on-prem appliance if required.

- BYOK / KMS: We support customer-managed keys via standard KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can do HSM-backed keys for Dedicated/Private. We also support Bring-Your-Own-Key with attested HSM providers — details in the security appendix (SOC2_Redwood_summary.pdf attached).

- Audit logs & formats: We can emit request-level audit events (request id, timestamp, caller identity, model id, model version, response metadata). We can export logs to your SIEM via syslog/HTTPS and also provide NDJSON dumps for discrete forensic exports. Default request log retention is 90 days for hosted accounts; retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private deployments and can be set to 180 days or longer per contract.

- KV cache & deletion: KV caches store transient conversation state; we can support policy-driven TTLs and explicit deletion APIs that scrub caches and invalidate persisted prefixes. For guaranteed scoped deletion across all layers we recommend Private + contractual verification steps, and we'll include deletion playbook steps in the appendix.

Action: I'll produce MAP_HealthTech_v0.2 with the appendix (audit schema, KMS options, retention knobs) and circulate by Monday (2026-03-30).

-Marissa
